title: Runtime compatibility stewardship: version lifecycle, LTS cadence, and safe-migration tools
creator: Samir Patel
body:
Summary: This ticket defines a pragmatic Runtime Semantic Versioning policy we call 'Compatibility Stewardship' and delivers the initial automation and observability needed to enact it. The goal is to make breaking changes explicit and rare, provide predictable deprecation timelines for downstream consumers (hosted API, Dedicated, Private), and ship a migration helper (CLI + CI checks) that lowers the cost of upgrades for customers and internal clients.

Motivation: We see recurring friction during upgrades: consumer client libraries fail silently when runtime behavior subtly changes, ops teams wrestle with ad-hoc rollouts, and customers delay upgrades due to unclear impact and migration effort. This work ties version semantics to rollout gates, telemetry, and automated adapters so upgrades are predictable and reversible.

Policy highlights (high-level):
- Major version (X.y.z): only for behavioral or contract-breaking changes. Behavioral change = change that can cause a previously successful request to fail or produce materially different structured output that downstream logic relies on (examples below).
- Minor version (x.Y.z): new, backward-compatible features, performance improvements that do not alter observable API behavior, opt-in capability flags, and additions to structured output that are additive and explicitly marked optional.
- Patch version (x.y.Z): bug fixes, non-functional improvements, documentation and telemetry changes, backwards-compatible performance changes.
- Deprecation headers: All runnable endpoints will return Deprecation-Window headers for deprecated fields/flags once a deprecation is announced. Default window: 90 days for hosted; 180 days for Dedicated/Private (with negotiation path).

Rollout gates and automation:
- Canary -> Staged -> Global rollout model with automated health gates. Canary population: 0.5% of traffic for 24h, staged increases to 10% for 48h, then 50% for 48h before global.
- Telemetry-driven gates: latency p50/p95/regression thresholds, error-rate (5xx) delta, quality-signal derived from our eval suite on a live shadow traffic slice. Gate triggers are codified in the rollout job.
- Automatic rollback: if any gate trips (above threshold for a window), rollout pauses and auto-rolls back after a 30m human-check window unless manually overridden.

Safe-migration tools we will deliver:
- compatibility-assertor GH Action (runtime/ci): runs a compatibility lint between runtime branches using a curated request corpus. Produces a compatibility report and a compatibility-score.
- migration-assistant CLI (rwm - redwood runtime migrator): takes a client codebase or prompt set and reports potential breakpoints + suggested adapters (e.g., automatically insert a response field shim, adjust expected tokenization flags).
- client-adapter-generator: server-side component that can produce small client adapters (JS/Go/Python snippets) to normalize responses for older client versions.

Observability and customer communication:
- New Grafana dashboards: compatibility-regressions, rollout-health, migration-requests-by-customer.
- Confluence playbook with canned communications and migration steps per customer tier (self-serve, dedicated support, enterprise concierge).
- Release note template that includes: change classification (behavioral|additive|patch), compatibility score, migration complexity estimate, and sample adapter snippet.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Artifacts & links: see links and related_prs fields.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Strict enforcement of behavioral-major rules delays product ship cadence. Trade-off: we will permit experimental flags (flag-perf/flag-alpha) behind runtime feature flags which can be promoted after stabilization.
- Migration tooling may not cover every custom downstream parser; we need a customer concierge program for enterprise customers.

Current progress (updates):
- 2026-02-12: Draft policy reviewed with Release Eng and Platform Product; action items captured.
- 2026-02-18: Compatibility-assertor prototype landed (GH CI prototype) and ran against feature/kv-cache-refactor branch. Initial compatibility-score metric designed.
- 2026-02-25: Decided on 90/180-day deprecation windows for hosted vs Dedicated/Private after legal + sales input.
- 2026-03-02: Migration-assistant CLI scoping complete; engineering spike in progress.
- 2026-03-08: Security review kickoff scheduled; preliminary threat model added.

Next steps: finalize policy doc, implement compatibility-assertor as an enforced CI gate for merges targeting main, ship rwm alpha for internal services, and add rollout gate automation into the deployment pipeline (k8s operator).
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc published in Confluence and linked from runtime repo README
compatibility-assertor GH Action blocks merges with compatibility-score below threshold (configurable)
rwm (migration-assistant) alpha released and used to generate at least 3 adapter snippets for internal clients
Rollout job updated to include telemetry gates and automatic rollback behavior
Dashboards for compatibility regressions live in Grafana and wired to alerting channels
decision_log: 2026-02-15: Adopted 'behavioral change' definition that includes structured-output incompatibility and semantic tokenization changes
2026-02-25: Agreed deprecation windows (90/180 days) after input from Sales & Legal
2026-03-03: Opted to gate major-version changes behind two positive canary cycles and one cross-team review approval
notes: Design trade-off: we will not attempt to automatically rewrite customer inference prompts. rwm will surface likely breakpoints and emit adapter suggestions instead.
Operational note: Dedicated/Private customers can opt into accelerated deprecation timelines via contract amendment.
Follow-up: schedule a customer webinar once the migration-assistant alpha is out
